360 ONE WAM Earnings Call - Q2 FY27 
 
 Mr. Anil Mascarenhas - Sr. EVP, Communications, 360 ONE WAM: 
 Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to 360 ONE WAM's earnings call for 
Q2 FY27. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in listen-only mode. In case you 
wish to ask a question or require assistance during the call, kindly signal the host by 
tapping on the raised hand icon. Please note, this conference is being recorded.  
 On the call today, we have with us Mr. Karan Bhagat, MD and CEO, Mr. Yatin Shah, 
CEO of the Wealth Business, Mr. Anshuman Maheshwary, CEO of 360 ONE Alternates, 
and Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa, our CFO. I now hand it over to Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa to take 
this call forward. 
 Mr. Sanjay Wadhwa - Chief Financial Officer, 360 ONE WAM Limited: 
 Thank you, Anil. A very good evening to all the participants.  
 Starting with the macros, Q2 was a quarter of two halves for Indian equities. Benchmark 
indices stayed under pressure through the quarter, weighed down by persistent FPI 
selling, global rate concerns, and geopolitical uncertainty. At the same time, domestic 
flows and primary markets were remarkably resilient. Monthly SIP flows touched a 
record of ₹32,500 crores in September, and close to 70 companies raised ₹90,500 
crores through IPOs during the quarter, including the landmark listing of NSE. We 
continue to believe that the long-term tailwinds clearly outweigh the near-term 
concerns. Let me call out four of them: 
 
First, wealth creation in India. The UHNI segment continues to grow at 13 - 15%, 
and monetization events such as IPOs, block deals, stake sales, keep releasing 
liquidity to promoters and families. 
 
Second, the financialization of savings. SIPs, the newly launched SIF category, and 
democratization of AIFs are steadily expanding the investable pool.  
 
Third, the shift to professional wealth management. Clients increasingly want 
transparent, fee-based advice, and a growing number of family offices want curated 
access to opportunities.  
 
And fourth, global connectivity. Resident Indians want to invest globally, global 
institutions are refocusing on India, and Gift City is opening new opportunities in 
asset management and broking. 
 We remain mindful of the near-term challenges, including market volatility, competition, 
evolving regulation, and pressure on costs. Our response is to stay the course, give the 
right advice to our clients, while running the business in our shareholders' interest.

 Now, coming to our performance for the quarter, total AUMs stood at about ₹9 lakh 
crores, up 31% year-on-year. ARR AUMs stood at ₹3,53,000 crores, up 19.7% year-on-
year, and ARR net flows of ₹12,482 crores during the quarter, compared to ₹10,815 
crores in Q1. Clients with more than ₹10 crores of AUM are over ₹4,100 and account 
for 95% of our ex-custody wealth AUM.  
 Revenue from operations was ₹896 crores, up 17.5% year-on-year. ARR revenue grew 
27.5% y-o-y to ₹706 crores. ARR now contributes 79% of operating revenues, and ARR 
retention improved to 79 basis points from 74 basis points in Q1, driven by higher carry 
income for the quarter. Excluding carry income, the ARR retentions remained stable at 
67 basis points. During Q2, carried interest from third-party funds contributed 
approximately ₹60 crores. Transaction and brokerage income was ₹190 crores, down 
9.1% year-on-year. Other income was negative ₹44 crores this quarter, primarily on 
account of mark-to-market impact on our treasury investments. As a result, total 
revenue was ₹853 crores, up 4.8% year-on-year.  
 Total costs were ₹462 crores, up 15.5% year-on-year. Employee costs were ₹342 
crores, up 19.9%, and include a one-time impact of about ₹9 crores from restructuring 
of one of our businesses. Admin and other costs were ₹120 crores, up 4.6%. Our cost-
to-operating income ratio improved to 51.5% from ₹54.3 in Q1.  
 Operating PBT grew 19.7% year-on-year to ₹434 crores. Given the lower other income, 
PBT was ₹391 crores and PAT was ₹302 crores, against ₹316 crores in Q2 FY26. 
Tangible ROE stood at 16.9%. The board approved a second interim dividend of 7.5 per 
share.  
 The wealth business saw a strong quarter, backed by strong flows and higher retentions. 
ARR AUM grew 24.3% year-on-year to ₹2,52,627 crores. 360 ONE Plus, our advisory 
platform, has now crossed ₹1 lakh crores. The quarter saw net flows of ₹10,990 crores 
that were broad-based across engagement models. New client additions and deeper 
wallet share with existing clients contributed towards the flow. ARR revenue grew 40.5% 
year-on-year to ₹503 crores. Retention improved to 79 basis points from 71 basis points 
in Q1. Operating PBT grew 30.2% year-on-year to ₹326 crores. The UHNI franchise 
remains the firm's anchor with unchanged priorities, grow share of wallet, widen our 
reach beyond the metros, and be the first call for families after a liquidity event. That 
last point matters more than ever, given record IPO and monetization activity over the 
last few years. More clients are moving to portfolio-level advisory mandates, which 
make relationships deeper and stickier. The HNI business continues to scale as a natural 
extension of UHNI. It now manages over ₹8,000 crores at healthy retentions for over 
1,500 clients and about 60 relationship managers. With productivity improving and a 
growing feeder pipeline into UHNI, we expect the business to break even on direct costs 
soon. With the business reset behind us, ET money is now built for profitable growth. 
Its base of 5.5 lakh plus active users is being taken towards a full lifecycle digital wealth 
platform. Clients will choose upfront between distribution and subscription-based 
advisory, and AI-assisted advice will extend into affluent segments. The distribution 
segment of the business clocked ARR AUM of over ₹700 crores over the last nine 

 
 3
months. The expected synergies from 360 ONE capital are now visible. Large IP 
mandates drew meaningful revenue accretion alongside an active block deal calendar. 
With strong ECM pipeline and expansion in research coverage, the franchise is gaining 
scale and building a more durable revenue base. Our collaboration with UBS continues 
to progress across bidirectional client reference, cross-platform product access, and 
exchange of best practices.  
 In the asset management segment, ARR AUM stood at a little over ₹100,000 crores, up 
9.4% year-on-year. Net flows improved to ₹1,492 crores after the large SMA 
redemptions in Q1. ARR revenue was ₹203 crores with retentions of 79 basis points, 
and operating PBT was ₹108 crores. In alternates, AIF AUM grew 27.9% year-on-year 
to ₹58,139 crores. We are amongst the leaders in private equity and credit space in 
India. During the quarter, we launched and mobilized funds across categories, including 
multi-stage AI fund, defence and space fund, ARISE credit fund. The pipeline remains 
strong for the coming quarters. In public markets, fund performance was strengthened, 
and our SIF strategy has gained traction with Dyna-SIF AUM crossing ₹1,000 crores. 
We won our first European institutional mandate and received a top-up from an existing 
global mandate.  
 Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear in wealth, focus on adding new clients, raising 
RM productivity, and scaling reference across 360 ONE ecosystem. In asset 
management, we will keep sharpening our alternates offering, expand our institutional 
reach, diversify domestic distribution, and build out the SIF platform. And in 360 ONE 
capital, the priority is converting the ECM pipeline, strengthening the team, and 
expanding research coverage. All of this will be delivered with continued cost discipline 
and technology as a key lever.  
 COMPASS, our proprietary and governed AI layer, is live across wealth, asset 
management, and enterprise functions. It gives the RM a single integrated interface for 
research and product knowledge, market intelligence, prospecting, and pitch 
preparation. A 360-degree view of each client's family holdings, and portfolio, and 
service and business at risk alerts with next best actions. COMPASS runs entirely within 
360 ONE environment with strict access controls. Client data never goes outside, and 
no data is used to train external models. The aim is simple, more time with clients, and 
a platform that scales efficiently. We do not judge COMPASS on usage, but on definite 
outcomes, which is efficiency, commercial impact, quality, and control.
